Method.name: Run
Method.Description: Using a secure connection, writes an integer value to a specific node on an OPC UA server, and then subsequently resets the value of that node back to what it was originally. Notice that this function operates on a node also referenced in the subscription data feed example Examples.OPCUADS.SecureExample, and that the effects of this test can be seen in the output of that example when that data feed is enabled and sourcing data.
Method.Implementation:
#dim tSC As %Status = $$$OK #dim e As %Exception.AbstractException
Try {
set tSC = ##class(OPCUA.Utils).Initialize() Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC)
set tClient = ##class(OPCUA.Client).%New()
set tSC = tClient.Initialize() Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC)
set tClientURI = "urn:secuac" set tCertificatePathname = "/usr/irissys/uac/certs/secuac.crt.der" set tPrivateKeyPathname = "/usr/irissys/uac/certs/secuac.key.der" set tTrustListDir = "/usr/irissys/uac/certs/trustdir" set tRevocationListDir = "/usr/irissys/uac/certs/crldir" set tSC = tClient.SetupClient(,$$$OpcuaMessageSecurityModeSignAndEncrypt,tClientURI,tCertificatePathname,tPrivateKeyPathname,tTrustListDir,tRevocationListDir) Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC)
set tSC = tClient.Connect("opc.tcp://certified-server","user1","password") Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC)
#dim tResults as %List
w !!, "Reading data (0): " set tSC = tClient.ReadValueAttribute(.tResults, "the.answer", 1, $$$OpcuaNodeIdTypeString) Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC)
zw tResults
set tValue = $LI(tResults,5)
w "Writing 57... " set tSC = tClient.WriteValueAttribute(57, $$$OpcuaDataTypeInt32, "the.answer", 1, $$$OpcuaNodeIdTypeString) Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC)
w "Reading data (1): " set tSC = tClient.ReadValueAttribute(.tResults, "the.answer", 1, $$$OpcuaNodeIdTypeString) Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC)
zw tResults
Hang 1
w "Writing 42... " set tSC = tClient.WriteValueAttribute(tValue, $$$OpcuaDataTypeInt32, "the.answer", 1, $$$OpcuaNodeIdTypeString) Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC)
w "Reading data (2): " set tSC = tClient.ReadValueAttribute(.tResults, "the.answer", 1, $$$OpcuaNodeIdTypeString) Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC)
zw tResults
w !!
set tSC = tClient.Disconnect()
} Catch (e) { Set tSC=e.AsStatus() }
Quit tSC

Method.name: Run
Method.Description: Writes each of an integer and a double value to a specific node on a publicly-accessible OPC UA server, and shows the change by reading values from the node beforehand and afterwards.
Method.Implementation:
#dim tSC As %Status = $$$OK #dim e As %Exception.AbstractException
Try {
set tSC = ##class(OPCUA.Utils).Initialize() Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC)
set tClient = ##class(OPCUA.Client).%New()
set tSC = tClient.Initialize() Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC)
set tSC = tClient.SetupClient() Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC)
set tSC = tClient.Connect("opc.tcp://opcuaserver.com:48010") Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC)
#dim tResults as %List #dim tValue as %Integer
w !!, "Temperature (0): " set tSC = tClient.ReadValueAttribute(.tResults, "AirConditioner_1.Temperature", 3, $$$OpcuaNodeIdTypeString) Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC) zw tResults
w "TemperatureSetPoint (0): " set tSC = tClient.ReadValueAttribute(.tResults, "AirConditioner_1.TemperatureSetPoint", 3, $$$OpcuaNodeIdTypeString) Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC) zw tResults
set tValue = 63 // Integer w "Writing "_tValue_"... " set tSC = tClient.WriteValueAttribute($DECIMAL(tValue), $$$OpcuaDataTypeUInt16, "AirConditioner_1.TemperatureSetPoint", 3, $$$OpcuaNodeIdTypeString) Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC)
w !, "Temperature (1): " set tSC = tClient.ReadValueAttribute(.tResults, "AirConditioner_1.Temperature", 3, $$$OpcuaNodeIdTypeString) Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC) zw tResults
w "TemperatureSetPoint (1): " set tSC = tClient.ReadValueAttribute(.tResults, "AirConditioner_1.TemperatureSetPoint", 3, $$$OpcuaNodeIdTypeString) Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC) zw tResults
w "Waiting 2 seconds..." Hang 2
set tValue = 731.5 // Double w !, "Writing "_tValue_"... " set tSC = tClient.WriteValueAttribute($DOUBLE(tValue), $$$OpcuaDataTypeDouble, "AirConditioner_1.TemperatureSetPoint", 3, $$$OpcuaNodeIdTypeString) Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC)
w !, "Temperature (2): " set tSC = tClient.ReadValueAttribute(.tResults, "AirConditioner_1.Temperature", 3, $$$OpcuaNodeIdTypeString) Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC) zw tResults
w "TemperatureSetPoint (2): " set tSC = tClient.ReadValueAttribute(.tResults, "AirConditioner_1.TemperatureSetPoint", 3, $$$OpcuaNodeIdTypeString) Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC) zw tResults
w !!
set tSC = tClient.Disconnect()
} Catch (e) { Set tSC=e.AsStatus() }
Quit tSC

Parameter.name: SETTINGS
Parameter.Description:
Configurable settings.
DataSourceClass renders as a dropdown of available device schemas, populated from the common superclass OPCUA.DataSource.DeviceSchema. Note that Ens.ContextSearch.SubclassOf takes the superclass in a parameter named "class" (not "super"), and already excludes abstract classes, so the abstract DeviceSchema base never appears in the list.

Property.name: URL
Property.Description: The URL of the server from which data is sought. (e.g. opc.tcp://servername:4840)

Property.name: ConnectionRetryTimeout
Property.Description: The duration (in seconds), since the last time that the OPC UA client was able to connect to the target OPC UA server, after which no more connection attempts will be made. If AlwaysConnect is checked, a warning will be issued instead

Property.name: AlwaysConnect
Property.Description: Indicates whether the OPC UA client should always attempt to connect to the target OPC UA server, regardless of any previous connection failures. If checked, a warning will be periodically issued after the duration specified in ConnectionRetryTimeout. On by default: unchecked, an outage longer than ConnectionRetryTimeout stops collection until the item is restarted, even once the server is back.

Property.name: DataSourceClass
Property.Description: The name of the DataSource class specifying the data types and nodes from which to obtain data as well as the fields in which to deposit the results.

Property.name: DeviceNodePaths
Property.Description:
The OPC UA device root nodes to read, one per line. Each line produces one table row per poll cycle, tagged with its NodePath.

Accepted forms per line:

  • ns=2;s=Plant.AC1 — string NodeId
  • ns=2;i=1047 — numeric NodeId
  • i=85 — NodeId in namespace 0
An optional label may follow a pipe, and becomes the NodePath value: ns=2;s=Plant.AC1|AC1. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored, so the list can be commented.

Each device is browsed at connect time and its children matched by name against the schema's columns, so adding a device is a one-line edit here — no regeneration and no recompile. Only used by the row-source services; the declarative Examples/Tests path ignores it.

Property.name: ClientURI
Property.Description: The "application URI" of this IRIS OPC UA connector. Notice that this identifying string may need to match comparable identifying strings noted within certificates used to identify this application to the target OPC UA server.

Property.name: PublicCertificate
Property.Description: The full pathname of the certificate that is to be used to identify the IRIS OPC UA connector as a client to the OPC UA server. Notice that this certificate may need to have been signed by a certicate authority that is trusted by the target OPC UA server. Should be supplied in DER format.

Property.name: PrivateKey
Property.Description: The full pathname of the private key that is to be used by this IRIS OPC UA connector in communications with the target OPC UA server. Should be supplied in DER format.

Property.name: TrustListDir
Property.Description: The full pathname of the directory in which the certificates of trusted sources are kept. Importantly, this directory may need to hold a valid certificate of the certificate authority that signs a target OPC UA server's identifying certificates, or a trusted certificate of a target OPC UA server itself. Certificates in this directory should be supplied in DER format.

Property.name: RevocationListDir
Property.Description: The full pathname of the directory in which certificate revocation lists (CRLs) are to be held. Such CRLs may be required for connecting to any given OPC UA server even in the event that no certificates have been revoked in regards to that server.

Property.name: LogFileTag
Property.Description: Indicates a tag that will identify a logfile for supplemental logging regarding this process. If omitted, supplemental logging will not be performed. Importantly, under some circumstances, use of this supplemental logging can result in a great amount of being written to disk and may result in degradation of application performance. Consequently, it is recommended that this feature only be used for the purposes of development and debugging and not for general system monitoring.

Method.name: OnInit
ApplyLogFile
Method.Description: Point the native library's log at <property>LogFileTag</property>. A failure is logged as a warning, not returned: the library log is a diagnostic aid, so it should not stop the service collecting data. Before, the status was overwritten by the next call and the failure went unseen.

Method.name: ConnectedState
Method.Description: The library's IsConnected flag for <var>pClient</var>, and its client reset flag in <var>pResetFlag</var>. Both are 0 when the state cannot be read: the enquiry leaves its outputs unset on failure, and a -1 placeholder left there counts as connected, so the polling adapter would never reconnect.

Method.name: Connect
ResolveSpecification
Method.Description:
Overridable hook, invoked by the concrete adapters once a live OPC UA session exists but before the read/subscription query is prepared.
Row-source services override this to browse each configured device and build the adapter Specification by matching node names — which is only possible with a live session, hence a hook here rather than work done in the service's OnInit(). It runs on every (re)connect, so a device that comes online after startup is picked up automatically.
The default is a deliberate no-op: the declarative v1 path (Examples, OPCUA.Tests) configures its Specification in OnInit() from the compiled class and must keep behaving exactly as before.
Method.Implementation: Quit $$$OK

Method.Description:

Shared by both row-source adapters' ResolveSpecification() overrides, so the polling and subscription paths cannot drift apart. Unresolved columns are logged once per (device, column) and stored as NULL.

Class.name: OPCUA.Adapter.TCPSubscriptionInboundAdapter
Class.Description: An inbound adapter for accessing data using an OPC UA subscription to monitored items on an OPC UA server.

Property.name: RequestedPublishingInterval
Property.Description: The requested cyclic rate (in milliseconds) that the Subscription is being requested to return Notifications to the Client. Notice that the actual rate is set by the server and may be different from that requested. If the requested value is 0 or negative, then the Server shall revise with the fastest supported publishing interval. Defined in section 5.13.2.2 of the OPC UA specification.

Property.name: RequestedLifetimeCount
Property.Description: When the publishing timer has expired this number of times without a Publish request being available to send a NotificationMessage, then the Subscription shall be deleted by the Server. Notice that the actual lifetime count is set by the server and may be different from that requested. The lifetime count must be a minimum of three times the keep keep-alive count. Defined in section 5.13.2.2 of the OPC UA specification.

Property.name: RequestedMaxKeepAliveCount
Property.Description: When the publishing timer has expired this number of times without requiring any NotificationMessage to be sent, the Subscription sends a keep-alive Message to the Client. Notice that the actual keep-alive count is set by the server and may be different from that requested. If the requested value is 0, the Server shall revise with the smallest supported keep-alive count. Defined in section 5.13.2.2 of the OPC UA specification.

Property.name: MaxNotificationsPerPublish
Property.Description: The maximum number of notifications that the Client wishes to receive in a single Publish response. A value of zero indicates that there is no limit. Defined in section 5.13.2.2 of the OPC UA specification.

Property.name: SubscriptionPollingTimeout
Property.Description: The timeout applied to each poll made by the client of the OPC UA server requesting notifications for changes to monitored items. Necessarily, the minimum time required to execute the poll.

Property.name: ReestablishOnEmptyResult
Property.Description: Indicates whether, in the event that no notifications are returned by the target server for a given subscription polling attempt, any existing connection to that server should be abandoned and an attempt made to reestablish the connection. A value of 1 indicates so; a value of 0 not. If indicated as a value higher than one, then the value also indicates the number of times that such subscription polling attempts must return no notifications before the connection should be abandoned and an attempt made to reestablish it.

Property.name: RequestedSamplingInterval
Property.Description: A duration in milliseconds indicating the interval at which monitored items on the server should be assessed by the server in order to determine if changes have occurred. A value of zero indicates that the server should use the fastest practical rate. A negative number indicates that the defualt rate should be used. Notice that the actual sampling intervals are set by the server and may be different than those requested. Notice also that, in this application, only a single rate may be requested and that that rate must be applicable to all monitored items for the subscription. Defined in section 7.16 of the OPC UA specification.

Property.name: RequestedQueueSize
Property.Description: Indicates the number of data changes that the server should remember, for any given monitored item, for reporting to the client when the client next polls asking for recent data changes. A value of one indicates that the server should keep track of only the most recent value, and any poll request by the client will be answered with only that most recent value regardless of how many times a data change has occurred since the time of the last poll of the server by the client. A value of zero indicates that the default quantity should be used. Notice that, in this application, only a single queue size may be requested and that requested queue size is assumed to be applicable to all monitored items for the subscription. Notice also that the actual queue sizes for monitored items on the server are set by the server and may be different than requested. Defined in section 7.16 of the OPC UA specification.

Property.name: RowSourceMasks
Property.Description: $LB($LB(1,0,1,...), ...) — per-device column coverage, discovered by browsing at connect time. Read by the row-source service to unpack notifications. Empty for the declarative path, which monitors a single fixed node set.

Property.name: RowSourcePaths
Property.Description: $LB(path1, path2, ...) — NodePath value per device, in the same order as <property>RowSourceMasks</property>.

Class.name: OPCUA.Client
Class.Description:
This class implements an interface to portions of the open source open62541 library, allowing for the creation of two different types of data feeds that can be used to import data into IRIS from OPC UA servers located locally, across a LAN, and/or over the Internet. Supports SecurityMode 1 (None: unencrypted, anonymous) and SecurityMode 3 (Sign & Encrypt: mutual TLS authentication with client certificate, private key, trust list and revocation list). Details about open62541 can be found at https://open62541.org. This client provides the ability to connect to an OPC UA server locally, across a LAN, or over the Internet.
  • Periodic Polling Data Feeds
    • -- Data feeds of this type are implemented as a simple request to an OPC UA server asking for a set of one or more node attributes to be returned. The query is first declared to this OPC UA client using ReadBulkSetup and subsequently, ReadBulkPoll can be used poll the server with a TCP/IP request in order to obtain the results representing a snapshot in time. ReadBulkPoll will return one complete row of results each time it is executed, and can be used as many times as is necessary. Later, when IRIS has finished using the feed, the query specification can be deleted from the client using the method ReadBulkClear.
  • Subscribing Data Feeds
    • -- Data feeds of this type are implemented using the OPC UA subscription framework whereby an OPC UA server is tasked with monitoring one or more variables held within it, and reporting any changes to those variables back to the requesting client. Feeds of this type can be declared using CreateSubscriptionSet, and subsequently, the client may request notfication of any recent changes with PollSubscriptionSet. Later, when IRIS has finisihed using the feed, the subscription can be deleted on the server using DeleteSubscriptionSet.

Method.name: ReadBulkSetup
Method.Description:
Prepares a query that can be subsequently executed repeatedly. The data elements requested are specified in four lists of equal length:
  • NodeTypes -- A list of numeric values indicating the type of node id that is used to identify the node. (e.g. $$$OpcuaNodeIdTypeString means a string is used to identify the node.)
  • NodeNamespaces -- A list of numeric values indicating the namespace for each requested node.
  • NodeIds -- A list of numeric or string values indicating the primary identifier used to identify each requested node.
  • NodeAttributes -- A kist of numeric values indicating the attribute to be returned for each requested node. (e.g. $$$OpcuaAttributeValue means that the value attribute should be returned.)
The QueryHandle is an output parameter that can subsequently be used to identify this particular query so that it can be executed and results for it obtained; this function simply declares the query. (This function is not deprecated, but ReadBulkSetupC is preferred.)

Method.name: ReadBulkSetupB
Method.Description: [DEPRECATED] Prepares a query that can be subsequently executed repeatedly. The data elements requested are specified in two lists of equal length, a a list of lists representing serialized node id objects, and a numeric list of attribute identifiers. (This function is deprecated; <method>ReadBulkSetupC</method> is preferred.)
Method.Implementation:
#dim tSC As %Status = $$$OK #dim e As %Exception.AbstractException
Try {
#dim NodeIdCLs as %List
Set NodeIdCLs = NodeIds
#; Call the library entry point Set tRetval=$ZF(-5,%ZUtilsIrisOpcuaLibraryId,$$$zfReadBulkSetupB,"",$LB(..Handle,NodeIdCLs,NodeAttributes))
#; Test for error condition If $List(tRetval,1)'=0 Set tSC=..DecodeError(tRetval) Quit
#; Set output variables Set QueryHandle = $LI(tRetval,2)
} Catch (e) { Set tSC=e.AsStatus() } Quit tSC

Method.name: ReadBulkSetupC
Method.Description:
Prepares a query that can be subsequently executed repeatedly. Data elements requested are detailed in a particular specification format that is the output of the OPCUA.DataSource framework. Such specifications are in the form of multidimensional lists which feature three top-level elements: (1) the DataSource name, (2) the name of the global on which the results will be saved, and (3) a multidimensional sublist identifying the property elements. For the purposes of this function, only the sublist of element three is relevant. That sublist begins with an empty element, which is then followed by other elements, each further element itself being a list, that list with the elements:
  • The type of the element: 1 = primitive, 2 = standard OPC UA
  • One as pPropertyPath_"."_oProp.Name e.g. "[MyDataSource2].Temperature"
  • The namespace
  • The node name or number
  • The attribute id number
For the purposes of this function, only the last three elements---the namespace, the node name/number, and attribute id---are relevant.

Method.name: ReadBulkPoll
Method.Description: Executes a query previously prepared with either ReadBulkSetup(), ReadBulkSetupB(), or ReadBulkSetupC(). Results are returned as a <class>%List</class> of primitives without time stamps. (This function is not deprecated, but <method>ReadBulkPollC</method> is preferred.)

Method.name: ReadBulkPollB
Method.Description: Executes a query previously prepared with either ReadBulkSetup() ReadBulkSetupB(), or ReadBulkSetupC(). Results are returned as a <class>%List</class> of <class>%List</class> for where each sublist consists of a requested primitive accompanied by its source timestamp. (This function is not deprecated, but <method>ReadBulkPollC</method> is preferred.)

Method.name: ReadBulkPollC
Method.Description: Executes a query previously prepared with either ReadBulkSetup() ReadBulkSetupB(), or ReadBulkSetupC(). Results are returned as a <class>%List</class> where each returned element is a <class>%List</class> representing a subclass of <class>OPCUA.Types.AbstractDataValue</class>.

Method.name: ReadBulkClear
Method.Description: Deletes a previously prepared query specification.

Method.name: CreateSubscriptionSet
Method.Description: [DEPRECATED] Creates and OPC UA subscription so as to receive updates regarding changes made to monitored items on a server. The data elements requested are specified in two lists of equal length, a list of lists representing serialized node id objects, and a numeric list of attribute identifiers. (This function is deprecated; <method>CreateSubscriptionSetB</method> is preferred.)
Method.Implementation:
#dim tSC As %Status = $$$OK #dim e As %Exception.AbstractException
Try {
#dim NodeIdCLs as %List
Set NodeIdCLs = NodeIds
#; Call the library entry point Set tRetval=$ZF(-5,%ZUtilsIrisOpcuaLibraryId,$$$zfCreateSubscription,"",$LB(..Handle,NodeIdCLs,NodeAttributes,PublishingInterval,LifetimeCount,MaxKeepAliveCount,MaxNotificationsPerPublish))
#; Test for error condition If $List(tRetval,1)'=0 Set tSC=..DecodeError(tRetval) Quit
#; Set output variables Set QueryHandle = $LI(tRetval,2) Set PublishingInterval = $LI(tRetval,3) // server-accepted value Set LifetimeCount = $LI(tRetval,4) // server-accepted value Set MaxKeepAliveCount = $LI(tRetval,5) // server-accepted value
} Catch (e) { Set tSC=e.AsStatus() } Quit tSC

Method.name: CreateSubscriptionSetB
Method.Description: Creates an OPC UA subscription so as to receive updates regarding changes made to monitored items on a server. Data elements for which notifications are requested are detailed in a particular specification format that is the output of the OPCUA.DataSource framework. The details of this format are the same as those indicated regarding the ReadBulkSetupC() function. The last four arguments of this function, the PublishingInterval, the LifetimeCount, the MaxKeepAliveCount, and the MaxNotificationsPerPublish are defined in section 5.13.2.2 of the OPC UA specification.

Method.name: PollSubscriptionSet
Method.Description: Polls a server for changes to a subscription set that has already been created using <method>CreateSubscriptionSet</method> or <method>CreateSubscriptionSetB</method>. Results are returned as a <class>%List</class> of <class>%List</class> for where each sublist consists of an output list of elements similar to that from the polling utility. Notice, here, that it is the sublist, and not the main list that bears resemblance to the output of some of the polling functions. This is because, unlike the polling functions, this function can return multiple rows per invocation.

Method.name: DeleteSubscriptionSet
Method.Description:
Deletes a set of subscriptions with a given server.
Needs the native library built on 2026-10-21 or later. Older builds freed the subscription here but kept a pointer to it, and freed it again when the client was reset or closed, which killed the process (signal 11).
Before a disconnect it is not needed. <method>Disconnect</method> closes the session with deleteSubscriptions = true, so the server drops every subscription.

Class.name: OPCUA.DataSource.Definition
Class.Description:
Base class for hand-authored "DataSource" classes: declare one typed property per OPC UA node (using the OPCUA.Types.* value classes plus OPCUANODENAME) and extend this class to map a node graph to an IRIS table. These declarative DataSources run under <class>TCPPollingService</class> / <class>TCPSubscriptionService</class> and are used by the Examples and the OPCUA.Tests harness (which validate the C++ type marshalling end-to-end).
NOTE: The pipeline wizard / REST /deploy endpoint does NOT use this path — it generates flat row-source classes consumed by the *RowSourceService runtime instead. See OPCUA.REST.DeployService and ARCHITECTURE.md.

Class.name: OPCUA.DataSource.DeviceSchema
Class.Description:
Common superclass for row-source device schemas (PRD "Baustein 1").
A device schema describes ONE device type — its columns and the OPC UA node names they resolve against — and carries no reference to any concrete device. The same schema is reused across N identical devices; the binding to a device is just an OPC UA node path, supplied at runtime via the adapter's DeviceNodePaths setting and resolved by name (see OPCUA.DataSource.Resolver).
Every schema generated by the wizard or by the /schemas REST endpoint extends this class. Beyond what it inherits from <class>OPCUA.DataSource.Definition</class>, its purpose is to give the DataSourceClass setting a precise, filterable class family for its Production Configuration dropdown: narrowing the dropdown to this class excludes the hand-authored Examples and OPCUA.Tests classes, which also extend Definition but would fail in a row-source service.

Class.name: OPCUA.DataSource.Generator
Class.Description: Auto-generates DataSource class definitions by browsing an OPC UA server. Connects to the server, walks the node tree depth-first from a start node, and produces a ready-to-use .cls file with properties mapped to discovered variable nodes. Types come from each node's DataType and ValueRank attributes (see InferType). Review the generated file and adjust any types that could not be determined. Terminal-only, and not part of the pipeline path. This writes a OPCUA.DataSource.Definition subclass to a .cls file for a human to review and import -- the declarative style the Examples and Tests use. It is not how pipelines are built: OPCUA.REST.SchemaService generates a OPCUA.DataSource.DeviceSchema subclass through the %Dictionary API and compiles it in place, with no file and no manual step. The `/generate` REST endpoint that used to expose this was removed with the Chrome extension, its only consumer. Two of its helpers are still on the live path and must not be moved: InferType (used by OPCUA.REST.ReadService to type a column) and SanitizePropertyName (used by OPCUA.REST.SchemaService to turn OPC UA names into legal property identifiers). Example usage: do ##class(OPCUA.DataSource.Generator).Generate( "opc.tcp://plc", 0, 84, "Generated.PLCDataSource", "PLCData", "/usr/irissys/mgr/User/")

Method.name: Generate
Method.Description:
Generate a DataSource class file by browsing an OPC UA server.
  • URL - OPC UA server URL (e.g., "opc.tcp://plc")
  • StartNodeNS - Namespace of the start node to browse from
  • StartNodeId - Node ID of the start node (e.g., 84 for Root)
  • ClassName - Fully qualified class name to generate
  • DataSourceName - Value for the OPCUADATASOURCE parameter
  • OutputPath - Directory to write the generated .cls file
  • StartNodeIdType - Node ID type of start node (0=numeric, 3=string)
  • SecurityMode - OPC UA security mode (1=None, 3=SignAndEncrypt)
  • MaxDepth - Maximum recursion depth for browsing (default 20)
  • Username - Optional username for authenticated connections
  • Password - Optional password for authenticated connections

Method.name: InferType
Method.Description:
Type a node from what the server declares about it, rather than from what its current value happens to look like.
Reads two attributes of the node: DataType (14), which names the type, and ValueRank (15), which says scalar, array or matrix. That settles the cases a value cannot: the native layer renders a Boolean as 0/1 like any integer, and a Double of 0.0 as "0". The value is read only when the server leaves the shape open (ValueRank Any / ScalarOrOneDimension), and the old value-based guess, <method>InferTypeFromValue</method>, is used only for a DataType that <method>MapDataTypeToIRIS</method> does not know -- a vendor-defined type, say.
The single-attribute read in the native layer supports only the Value attribute, so the attributes are fetched as a one-shot bulk query (<method>ReadAttributesOnce</method>). DataType and ValueRank share one query and the Value, when needed, gets its own: a value of a type the native layer cannot convert (a Guid, an ExtensionObject) fails the whole poll, while DataType and ValueRank are always a NodeId and an integer.

Method.name: ReadTypeAttributes
Method.Description: Fetch a node's DataType and ValueRank. Returns 0 if either is unavailable -- the node does not exist, or is not a variable. pDataType is the numeric id of a namespace-0 type, or "" for a type defined in another namespace.

Method.name: ValueDimensions
Method.Description:
Number of dimensions the node's current value actually has: 0 for a scalar, 1 for an array, 2 for a matrix. Used only when ValueRank leaves it open. A value that cannot be read counts as a scalar.
This cannot use <method>OPCUA.Client.ReadValueAttribute</method>: the native single read returns an array value as null. The bulk read returns it intact.
Method.Implementation: Quit:'..ReadAttributesOnce(pClient, pNodeNS, pNodeId, $LB($$$OpcuaAttributeValue), .tResults) 0 // $LB(sourceTS, serverTS, status, value[, dimensions]) set tDV = $ListGet(tResults, 1) Quit:'$ListValid(tDV)||($ListLength(tDV) < 4) 0 set tValue = $ListGet(tDV, 4) // An empty String reads back as an empty list, so only a non-empty list is an array. Quit:'$ListValid(tValue)||($ListLength(tValue) = 0) 0 Quit $Select($ListValid($ListGet(tValue, 1)) && ($ListGet(tValue, 1) '= ""):2, 1:1)

Method.name: ReadAttributesOnce
Method.Description: Read some attributes of one node as a one-shot bulk query: ReadBulkSetupC, one ReadBulkPollC, ReadBulkClear. pResults holds one entry per attribute in pAttributes, "" for any the server did not return. Returns 0 if the query itself failed -- including when a value cannot be converted, which fails the whole poll, so callers keep attributes that might not convert in a query of their own.

Method.name: MapDataTypeToIRIS
Method.Description: Map an OPC UA DataType to an OPCUA.Types class. pTypeNodeId is the numeric id of a namespace-0 type (1 = Boolean ... 13 = DateTime, 21 = LocalizedText). pDimensions is 0 for a scalar, 1 for an array, 2+ for a matrix. Returns "" for a type this does not know, so the caller can fall back.

Method.name: InferTypeFromValue
Method.Description: Guess the IRIS OPCUA.Types class from the node's current value. This is the fallback behind <method>InferType</method>, for nodes whose declared DataType is unknown to <method>MapDataTypeToIRIS</method>; it cannot tell a Boolean from an integer, nor a Double of 0.0 from one. Falls back to StringDataValue if the value is null or unreadable.

Class.name: OPCUA.DataSource.Resolver
Class.Description:
Resolve a device schema plus a device list into a concrete adapter specification, by browsing each device and matching its children by name against the schema's OPCUANODENAME parameters (PRD "Baustein 2").
This is what replaces the frozen absolute node IDs that the wizard used to capture at deploy time and store in ^OPCUA.RowSource: a device binding is now just a node path, and the concrete node IDs behind each column are discovered at connect time. A device that comes online, or gains a node, between two connects is therefore picked up automatically.
Matching is by name, preferring the stable BrowseName and falling back to the localized DisplayName (schemas generated by the wizard populate OPCUANODENAME from DisplayName, so the fallback is what makes existing schemas resolve). A column whose node is absent simply gets mask bit 0 and stores NULL, which preserves the semantics of the old precomputed column masks.

Method.name: ParseDeviceNodePaths
Method.Description:
Parse the DeviceNodePaths setting into a device list.
One device per line. Accepted forms per line: ns=2;s=Plant.AC1 → string NodeId ns=2;i=1047 → numeric NodeId i=85 / s=Foo → NodeId in namespace 0 An optional label may follow a pipe, and becomes the NodePath column value: ns=2;s=Plant.AC1|AC1 → NodePath reads "AC1" Without a label the NodePath column holds the nodepath as written.
Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored, so a device list can be commented. Lines are separated by LF, CR or CRLF.
Output: pDevices = $LB($LB(ns, id, idType, label), ...)

Method.name: ParseNodePath
Method.Description: Parse one nodepath into namespace, identifier and identifier type. Supports the OPC UA textual NodeId forms "ns=<n>;s=<string>" and "ns=<n>;i=<int>", with the ns= part optional (defaults to namespace 0).

Method.name: GetSchemaColumns
Method.Description:
Read the schema's column layout from the compiled class.
Walks ^OPCUA.DataSource(schemaClass) — written by <class>OPCUA.DataSource.Projection</class> at compile time — in storage order, which is exactly the order the runtime services index columns by, so mask index and column index stay aligned.
Output: pColumns(i) = $LB(propertyPath, namespace, nodeName, attributeId, folderName) where folderName is "" for a flat column, or the OPCUANODENAME of the enclosing %SerialObject folder for a nested one. Nested columns must be resolved one level deeper, under their folder's node.

Method.name: MapSerialFolders
Method.Description: Build a map of property path → OPC UA node name for every %SerialObject folder property in the schema class. Used to attribute nested columns to their folder, and by the runtime services to derive the nesting layout.

Method.name: DeriveNestingSpec
Method.Description:
Derive the nesting layout for a schema from its compiled class.
The row-source services need to know how flat leaf values map onto the %SerialObject structure of a storage row. That layout used to be precomputed at deploy time and stored in ^OPCUA.RowSource; it is instead derived here from the class itself, which cannot go stale.
Walks the class's storage order (the same order the column masks use) and emits one entry per storage slot: $LB("leaf", leafIndex) — a direct value $LB("serial", folderName, innerSpec) — an embedded serial object where innerSpec is a list of $LB("leaf", leafIndex) for the folder's own properties, in the serial class's storage order.
leafIndex numbering matches the order GetSchemaColumns() reports columns in, so the services can index resolved values directly.
Returns "" when the schema has no nested folders (flat layout).
pLeafTypes is the property type of each leaf, in the same leaf order, and is filled for flat schemas too. RowWriter uses it to tell measurements that keep their server timestamp from those that do not.

Method.name: IsMeasurementType
Method.Description: Is this property type a measurement (an OPCUA.Types DataValue, with or without its server timestamp) rather than a folder or a plain value?

Method.Description: Is this a measurement type stored without its server timestamp?

Method.name: ResolveSpecification
Method.Description:
Resolve a schema and a device list into a concrete adapter specification by browsing each device and matching children by name against OPCUANODENAME.
pClient must already be connected — browsing needs a live session, which is why resolution happens from the adapter's Connect() rather than the service's OnInit(). See OPCUA.Adapter.Common.ResolveSpecification().
Outputs: pSpec combined specification for ReadBulkSetupC / CreateSubscriptionSetB, shaped exactly like the one the Projection produces: $LB(dsName, storageGlobal, $LB("", entry1, entry2, ...)) with one entry per resolved column per device, devices in order pMasks $LB($LB(1,0,1,...), ...) — one discovered coverage mask per device, in schema column order; bit 0 means "no such node on this device" pDiagnostics $LB($LB(deviceLabel, columnNodeName, reason), ...) — unresolved columns, for the caller to log

Method.name: BrowseIntoMap
Method.Description:
Browse one node and index its children by name for lookup.
Both BrowseName and DisplayName are indexed, BrowseName winning when the two disagree, so a schema whose OPCUANODENAME came from either one still resolves. A duplicate name keeps the first match, deterministically (PRD risk table).
Output: pMap(nameKey) = $LB(ns, id, idType)

Method.name: NameKey
Method.Description:
Build the lookup key for a node name.
The key is the name itself: matching is exact and case-sensitive, as OPC UA BrowseNames are. Do not strip a "<namespaceIndex>:" prefix. The native library delivers a BrowseName as $LB(name, nsIndex), so no prefix ever arrives, and stripping one turned a digits-only name ("42") into an empty subscript and "10:30 Shift" into "30 Shift".
Method.Implementation: pName

Class.name: OPCUA.DataSource.RowWriter

Property.name: RowSize

Method.name: BuildNestedValues

Class.name: OPCUA.REST.BrowseService
Class.Description: Browse OPC UA node children and return JSON array for lazy-loading tree.

Method.name: Browse
Method.Description:
Browse children of the specified node. Input: pBody with url, optional nodeNs (default 0), nodeId (default 84=Root/Objects), nodeIdType (default 0=numeric), probeChildren (default 1) Returns a %DynamicArray of child node objects.
<var>probeChildren</var> spends a second, batched browse to make each child's <var>hasChildren</var> true rather than guessed -- see <method>ProbeChildCounts</method>. Pass 0 to skip it when only names and ids are wanted and a wrong expand arrow costs nothing.

Method.name: WalkBrowseResults
Method.Description:
Walk the raw browse result list from the C++ layer and return one entry per child reference. This is the single shared decoding of the C++ browse wire format: <method>ParseBrowseResults</method> renders it as JSON for the REST API, and <class>OPCUA.DataSource.Resolver</class> uses it to match children by name at runtime. Keeping one walk means the REST and runtime views of a server cannot drift apart.
C++ browse reference list positions: [1] referenceTypeId (NodeId: ns, id, idType) [2] isForward (boolean) [3] nodeId (ExpandedNodeId: ns, id, idType, ...) [4] browseName (QualifiedName: name, ns) [5] displayName (LocalizedText: text, locale) [6] nodeClass (UA_NodeClass as Int32 — see <method>ClassifyNode</method>) [7] typeDefinition (ExpandedNodeId: ns, id, idType, ...)
Output: pChildren(i) = $LB(browseName, displayName, ns, id, idType, category, refType, nodeClass) where browseName and displayName are kept SEPARATE (unlike the JSON view, which collapses them) because name-based resolution prefers the stable BrowseName. nodeClass is appended last so existing callers reading positions 1-7 are unaffected.

Method.name: ParseBrowseResults
Method.Description: Parse raw browse results from C++ layer into a %DynamicArray of node objects. Uses the 3-axis classification model: nodeClass + referenceType + typeDefinition. Decoding is delegated to <method>WalkBrowseResults</method>; this method only shapes the result as JSON for the REST API.

Method.name: CountChildReferences
Method.Description: Count the real children in one raw browse result, applying the same non-child filter as <method>WalkBrowseResults</method>.

Method.name: ProbeChildCounts
Method.Description:
Replace the guessed <var>hasChildren</var> on each node with the truth.
A browse response says what a node *is*, never whether it has children, so <method>CategoryHasChildren</method> can only guess from the category -- and it guesses optimistically, marking every variable expandable because some variables really do carry child properties (EURange under an AnalogItemType). On a server whose tags are bare, that draws an expand arrow on every leaf which then opens to nothing.
The fix is one extra browse, batched: <method>OPCUA.Client.Browse</method> takes lists, so all N siblings are probed in a single round trip and the grandchildren are counted and discarded. Cost is 2 round trips per expand instead of 1, not N+1, and depth stays lazy -- this looks exactly one level past what is being rendered, never deeper.
Best-effort by design. If the probe fails, or the server returns a result count that does not line up with what was asked, the guessed values stand: an arrow that opens to nothing is a smaller failure than a node the user cannot open.

Method.name: IsNonChildReference
Method.Description:
Is this reference something other than a child of the browsed node?
HasTypeDefinition (40) points at the node's *type*, and HasSubtype (45) at its place in a type hierarchy; neither is a child in the tree sense. Every bare variable carries a HasTypeDefinition, so counting references without this filter makes every leaf look like it has exactly one child.
Extracted so <method>WalkBrowseResults</method> and <method>CountChildReferences</method> apply the same rule -- if they disagreed, the expand arrow would contradict what expanding actually shows.
Method.Implementation: if pRefTypeNS '= 0 Quit 0 Quit (pRefTypeId = 40) || (pRefTypeId = 45)

Method.name: ClassifyReferenceType
Method.Description: Classify the reference type from its NodeId. Standard reference type IDs (ns=0): 35=Organizes, 46=HasProperty, 47=HasComponent, 49=HasOrderedComponent 44=Aggregates, 36=HasEventSource, 48=HasNotifier
Method.Implementation: if pNS '= 0 Quit "HasComponent" if pId = 46 Quit "HasProperty" if pId = 35 Quit "Organizes" if (pId = 47) || (pId = 49) Quit "HasComponent" if pId = 36 Quit "HasEventSource" if pId = 48 Quit "HasNotifier" // Other hierarchical references default to HasComponent Quit "HasComponent"

Method.name: ClassifyNode
Method.Description:
Classify a node into a UI category using nodeClass + referenceType + typeDefinition. Categories: "folder", "object", "variable", "property", "method". A View is reported as "folder", since to a browsing user it behaves as one.
pNodeClass is the server's own UA_NodeClass, and it is authoritative about the coarse kind — a Method is a Method no matter what references point at it. Where OPC UA's node classes are coarser than the categories this UI needs, the older TypeDefinition heuristics still do the refining: Object splits into folder-vs-object, Variable into variable-vs-property.
It stays optional. Prebuilt binaries older than the <method>UA2CL_ReferenceDescription</method> nodeClass export send "" here, so an empty value falls through to inferring the kind exactly as before.
UA_NodeClass values: 1=Object, 2=Variable, 4=Method, 8=ObjectType, 16=VariableType, 32=ReferenceType, 64=DataType, 128=View
Key TypeDefinition IDs (ns=0): FolderType=61, BaseObjectType=58 BaseVariableType=62, BaseDataVariableType=63, PropertyType=68 DataItemType=2365, AnalogItemType=2368, DiscreteItemType=2372 TwoStateDiscreteType=2373, MultiStateDiscreteType=2376 See full list in research doc.

Method.name: IsVariableTypeDef
Method.Description: Check if a TypeDefinition ID (ns=0) is a variable type. Covers BaseVariableType, BaseDataVariableType, and all standard data-bearing VariableType subtypes from the OPC UA specification.

Method.name: CategoryHasChildren
Method.Description:
Guess whether a node category is expandable, from the category alone.
Optimistic on purpose: it is the value <method>ProbeChildCounts</method> overwrites with a measured one, and it is what survives when the probe is switched off or fails. Guessing "expandable" wrongly costs an arrow that opens to nothing; guessing "leaf" wrongly hides a subtree, which is worse.

Class.name: OPCUA.REST.ClientManager
Class.Description: Manages per-request OPC UA client lifecycle for REST endpoints. Creates a connected client, executes work, then disconnects.

Method.name: Connect
Method.Description: Create a connected OPC UA client from request parameters. Returns the client instance by reference; caller must call Disconnect() when done.

Method.name: Disconnect
Method.Description: Safely disconnect a client, ignoring errors.

Method.name: ExtractConnectionParams
Method.Description: Extract common connection parameters from a JSON request body. Returns URL by reference. Other params are optional with defaults.
Method.Implementation: set pURL = pBody.%Get("url") if pURL = "" { Quit $$$ERROR($$$GeneralError, "Missing required parameter: url") } set tSecVal = pBody.%Get("securityMode") set pSecurityMode = $Select(tSecVal="":1, +tSecVal=0:1, 1:+tSecVal) set tUser = pBody.%Get("username") set pUsername = $Select(tUser="":"", 1:tUser) set tPass = pBody.%Get("password") set pPassword = $Select(tPass="":"", 1:tPass) set tCert = pBody.%Get("certPath") set pCertPath = $Select(tCert="":"", 1:tCert) set tKey = pBody.%Get("keyPath") set pKeyPath = $Select(tKey="":"", 1:tKey) set tTrust = pBody.%Get("trustDir") set pTrustDir = $Select(tTrust="":"", 1:tTrust) set tCrl = pBody.%Get("crlDir") set pCrlDir = $Select(tCrl="":"", 1:tCrl) set tURI = pBody.%Get("clientURI") set pClientURI = $Select(tURI="":"", 1:tURI) Quit $$$OK

Class.name: OPCUA.REST.ConnectionService
Class.Description: Test OPC UA server connectivity and return response time.

Method.name: Test
Method.Description: Test connection to an OPC UA server. Input: pBody with url, optional securityMode, username, password Returns a %DynamicObject with connected status and response time in ms.

Class.name: OPCUA.REST.DeployService
Class.Description: Bind devices to an existing device schema: add a business service item to the shared production (OPCUA.Pipeline.Production), where each pipeline is a separate service item. This class generates nothing. Schemas are created by OPCUA.REST.SchemaService, and a deploy binds devices to one that already exists — which is what lets a schema outlive any single pipeline and back several at once. A deploy is a pure configuration write: the new item is created disabled and the production is not started. Collecting real data into a real table is a decision of its own, so it is left to an explicit start (OPCUA.REST.PipelineService.Toggle, or the Portal) once the operator has looked the pipeline over.

Parameter.name: ProductionClass
Parameter.Description: The shared production class that holds all pipeline service items.

Parameter.name: PipelineCategory
Parameter.Description: The Portal category every pipeline we create belongs to, alongside the short name of its schema. See <method>EnsureCategories</method>.

Method.name: Deploy
Method.Description: Deploy a pipeline: <tt>{schemaClass, devices, ...}</tt>. See <method>BindExistingSchema</method>.

Method.name: BindExistingSchema
Method.Description:
Bind devices to an existing schema, generating nothing. Adding a pipeline over a schema that already exists costs one config item and no compilation. Body: { schemaClass required, must be an OPCUA.DataSource.DeviceSchema subclass devices required, newline-separated nodepaths (DeviceNodePaths form) dataSourceName config item name; defaults to the schema's short name mode "polling" (default) or "subscription" url OPC UA endpoint callInterval polling mode, seconds (default 5) publishingInterval / samplingInterval / queueSize subscription mode, ms securityMode + clientURI, certPath, keyPath, trustDir, crlDir for mode 3 credentials optional: the ID of an existing Ens.Config.Credentials entry username, password optional, instead of credentials: saved as a new entry CredentialsId(name), never in a setting }

Neither credentials nor username means an anonymous session, and no entry. A password without a username is ignored, as an anonymous connect ignores it.

Method.name: EnsureProductionExists
Method.Description: Ensure the shared production class exists. Creates it on first deploy.
Method.Implementation:
if ##class(%Dictionary.ClassDefinition).%ExistsId(..#ProductionClass) { Quit $$$OK }
#dim tSC As %Status = $$$OK Try { set tClassDef = ##class(%Dictionary.ClassDefinition).%New(..#ProductionClass) set tClassDef.Description = "Shared OPC UA pipeline production. Service items are added automatically." set tClassDef.Super = "Ens.Production"
set tXData = ##class(%Dictionary.XDataDefinition).%New() set tXData.Name = "ProductionDefinition" do tXData.Data.Write("<Production Name="""_..#ProductionClass_""" LogGeneralTraceEvents=""false"">") do tXData.Data.Write("<Description>OPC UA Data Pipelines</Description>") do tXData.Data.Write("<ActorPoolSize>2</ActorPoolSize>") do tXData.Data.Write("</Production>") do tClassDef.XDatas.Insert(tXData)
set tSC = tClassDef.%Save() $$$ThrowOnError(tSC) set tSC = $System.OBJ.Compile(..#ProductionClass, "ck-d") $$$ThrowOnError(tSC) } Catch (e) { set tSC = e.AsStatus() } Quit tSC

Method.name: AddServiceItem
Method.Description:
Add a new business service item to the shared production using the Ens.Config API.
pDeviceNodePaths is used verbatim as the DeviceNodePaths setting; the caller has already parsed and validated it.

Method.name: CredentialsId
Method.Description:
The <tt>Ens.Config.Credentials</tt> ID deploy uses for the entry it creates for pipeline <var>pItemName</var>: <tt>OPCUA-</tt> plus the name.
Every character other than a letter, digit, dot, hyphen or underscore becomes <tt>_</tt>, so the ID reads cleanly in the Portal's credentials list and can never hold the <tt>||</tt> ID separator. The ID is at most 50 characters (<tt>SystemName</tt>'s MAXLEN), and pipeline names run to 128, so a longer one keeps its first 41 characters plus <tt>-</tt> and an 8-digit hex CRC of the full name, which keeps names that differ only at the end apart.
Two pipeline names can still map to one ID ("A B" and "A_B"). Deploy then refuses the second with 409, as it does for any taken ID.

Method.name: ResolveCredentials
Method.Description:
Check the body's credentials choice, and return in <var>pCheckBody</var> the body the coverage check connects with: the caller's own, or, for an existing entry, a copy carrying that entry's username and password.
400 if <tt>credentials</tt> names no entry, or comes with a <tt>username</tt> too. 403 if this IRIS account may not read the entry, or (with a <tt>username</tt>) may not create one. Nothing is created here; <method>AddServiceItem</method> does that.

Method.name: ReadCredentials
Method.Description:
The username and password in credentials entry <var>pId</var>, for a connect made on the caller's behalf (deploy's and rebind's coverage checks).
The ID is matched as Ens matches it: case-insensitively, and "" or <tt>none</tt> mean no credentials (an anonymous session). 400 if no entry has the ID. 403 if this IRIS account cannot read stored passwords: <tt>Ens.Config.Credentials</tt> then hands back an empty password with no error, and the connect would fail with a misleading BadUserAccessDenied.

Method.name: FindCredentialsId
Method.Description: The stored ID of the credentials entry whose ID matches <var>pId</var> in any case, as <tt>Ens.Config.Credentials.GetCredentialsObj</tt> matches it; "" when there is none.
Method.Implementation: Quit:pId="" "" set tLower = $ZConvert(pId, "L"), tId = "" &sql(SELECT TOP 1 SystemName INTO :tId FROM Ens_Config.Credentials WHERE LOWER(SystemName) = :tLower) Quit $Select(SQLCODE=0:tId, 1:"")

Method.name: CanReadCredentials
Method.Description: Whether this process may read stored credentials passwords. Ens keeps them in <tt>^Ens.SecondaryData.Password</tt>, in the namespace's secondary database, and reads them with no privilege check of its own, so a reference that raises <PROTECT> is the only reliable sign. The Portal also requires %Ens_Credentials to view credentials, so that is checked too.

Method.name: CanWriteCredentials
Method.Description: Whether this process may create and delete credentials entries: %Ens_Credentials:W, which <tt>%SYS.Ensemble</tt> checks before storing or removing a password.
Method.Implementation: $System.Security.Check(..#CredentialsResource, "W")

Parameter.name: CredentialsResource
Parameter.Description: The resource that guards credentials entries.

Method.name: NoCredentialsAccess
Method.Description: 403 for a credentials operation this IRIS account may not do. <var>pWhat</var> describes it ("read the password in credentials 'X'"), <var>pPermission</var> is the permission it needs on %Ens_Credentials.
Method.Implementation: Quit ##class(OPCUA.REST.Error).Forbidden("IRIS user '"_$Username_"' cannot "_pWhat_": that needs the "_..#CredentialsResource_" resource ("_pPermission_"), as SuperUser has. Sign the console in as a developer with SuperUser rights, or have an administrator create the credentials in the Management Portal and deploy with 'credentials'.")

Method.name: CreateOwnedCredentials
Method.Description:
Create credentials entry <var>pId</var> for pipeline <var>pItemName</var> and record that deploy made it, in <tt>^OPCUA.OwnedCredentials(pId)</tt>, so that deleting the pipeline deletes it and nothing else.
An existing entry is never overwritten, with one exception: our own leftover. A pipeline deleted in the Management Portal leaves its entry and our marker behind. When the marker names this same pipeline and no item in any production references the entry, it is ours and orphaned, so it is replaced. Any other existing entry is a 409.

Method.name: CredentialsUsers
Method.Description: The items, in any production of this namespace, whose Credentials setting names entry <var>pId</var> (in any case), as "Item (Production)" joined with ", " in <var>pUsers</var>; "" when none. Any failure is an error, so a caller never treats an entry as unused on a guess. Embedded SQL, which checks no SQL privilege.

Method.name: DeleteOwnedCredentials
Method.Description: Delete credentials entry <var>pId</var> if, and only if, deploy created it for pipeline <var>pItemName</var>. Any other entry is left alone. Returns OK when there is nothing of ours to delete.
Method.Implementation: Quit:'..OwnsCredentials(pId, pItemName) $$$OK Quit:'..CanWriteCredentials() ..NoCredentialsAccess("delete credentials '"_pId_"'", "W") if ##class(Ens.Config.Credentials).%ExistsId(pId) { set tSC = ##class(Ens.Config.Credentials).%DeleteId(pId) Quit:$$$ISERR(tSC) tSC } kill ^OPCUA.OwnedCredentials(pId) Quit $$$OK

Method.name: OwnsCredentials
Method.Description: Whether deploy created credentials entry <var>pId</var> for pipeline <var>pItemName</var>.
Method.Implementation: Quit:pId="" 0 Quit $Get(^OPCUA.OwnedCredentials(pId))=pItemName

Method.name: DuplicateNameError
Method.Description: The refusal for a pipeline name that is already taken.
Method.Implementation: Quit ##class(OPCUA.REST.Error).Conflict("A pipeline named '"_pName_"' already exists. Choose a different name.")

Method.name: NormalizeCategories
Method.Description:
Turn a caller-supplied category list into the comma-delimited string <tt>Ens.Config.Item.Category</tt> expects.
Accepts either a JSON array (what the console sends) or an already-joined comma string, so a hand-rolled request works too. Entries are trimmed, blanks dropped, and duplicates removed case-insensitively — the Portal treats categories as display strings, so "opcua" and "OPCUA" would otherwise show as two groups meaning one thing. The first spelling of a repeated name wins.
Commas inside a single entry are the one thing that cannot survive: the field is comma-delimited, so an entry containing one would silently split into two categories. They are stripped rather than escaped, because a category is a short label and there is nothing to escape *to*.

Method.name: DefaultCategories
Method.Description: The categories a freshly deployed pipeline gets when the caller does not name them: <tt>OPCUA</tt> plus the schema's short name. Exposed so the console can prefill its editor with exactly what the backend would have chosen.
Method.Implementation: set tSchemaName = $Piece(pSchemaClass, ".", *) set tOut = ..#PipelineCategory if tSchemaName '= "" set tOut = tOut_","_tSchemaName Quit tOut

Method.name: EnsureCategories
Method.Description:
Stamp a config item's Portal categories: <tt>OPCUA</tt> plus the short name of the schema it is bound to.
<tt>Ens.Config.Item.Category</tt> is a comma-delimited string, and <tt>Ens.Config.Production:EnumerateCategories</tt> strips whitespace around each piece — so the Portal's category filter sees these as two separate groups. Categories are organisational only; nothing in the runtime reads them back, so a missing category is cosmetic rather than a broken pipeline.
Existing categories are kept, and neither name is added twice, so this is safe to call on an item that has already been stamped.

Method.name: AddSetting
Method.Description: Add a setting to a config item.
Method.Implementation: set tSetting = ##class(Ens.Config.Setting).%New() set tSetting.Target = pTarget set tSetting.Name = pName set tSetting.Value = pValue do pItem.Settings.Insert(tSetting)

Method.name: AddSettingIfNotEmpty
Method.Description: Add a setting only if the JSON body has a non-empty value for the given key.

Method.name: StartOrUpdateProduction
Method.Description: Start the production, or update it if already running. Refuses, without stopping anything, while another production holds the namespace (see <method>CheckNoOtherProduction</method>).

Method.name: ValidateItemName
Method.Description: 400 unless <var>pName</var> ("" means the default, which is valid) can name a config item: Ens.Config.Item allows at most 128 characters and refuses some separators (<method>Ens.Config.Item.CheckForIllegalCharacters</method>). Checked up front so the caller gets a readable 400, not a failed save.

Method.name: CheckNoOtherProduction
Method.Description:
Error if a production other than ours holds this namespace.
A namespace runs one production at a time, so ours cannot start while another is running, suspended or troubled. That one may belong to someone else, so it is reported, not stopped.

Class.name: OPCUA.REST.Error
Class.Description:
Errors that carry the HTTP status the REST API answers with.
<method>Make</method> builds an ordinary <tt>$$$GeneralError</tt> whose second parameter is the HTTP code; the message text is unchanged, so service callers and tests see the same text as before. <method>HttpCode</method> reads it back. A plain <tt>$$$GeneralError</tt> is our own validation message, so it is 400. Anything else (an ObjectScript error, a %Dictionary or Ens error) is unexpected, so it is 500 and its text never goes into a response.

Method.name: Make
Method.Description: An error with the HTTP code <var>pHttp</var> and the readable <var>pMessage</var>. <var>pCause</var>, when given, is appended to the status: it is logged with a 500 but never shown.

Method.name: BadRequest
Method.Description: 400: the request itself is wrong.
Method.Implementation: Quit ..Make(400, pMessage)

Method.name: NotFound
Method.Description: 404: the named schema or pipeline does not exist.
Method.Implementation: Quit ..Make(404, pMessage)

Method.name: Forbidden
Method.Description: 403: the signed-in IRIS account lacks a privilege the request needs (for example %Ens_Credentials). Signing in again does not help, so it is not 401.
Method.Implementation: Quit ..Make(403, pMessage)

Method.name: Conflict
Method.Description: 409: the request is fine but clashes with current state (in use, name taken, another production running, edit lock busy, stale save).
Method.Implementation: Quit ..Make(409, pMessage)

Parameter.name: ValidationCodes
Parameter.Description: Error codes that say a value the caller supplied failed datatype validation: #5794 (type), #5802 (property) and #7201 (longer than MAXLEN). Their text names the value and the rule, nothing internal, so they are 400 and shown.

Method.name: HttpCode
Method.Description: The HTTP code for <var>pSC</var>: the code its first error carries, else 400 when every error in it is a plain <tt>$$$GeneralError</tt> or a datatype validation failure (<parameter>ValidationCodes</parameter>), else 500.

Method.name: IsValidationCode
Method.Implementation: (..#ValidationCodes [ (","_pCode_","))

Method.name: Carried
Method.Description: Whether the first error of <var>pSC</var> carries an explicit HTTP code, i.e. was built by <method>Make</method>.
Method.Implementation: Quit:$$$ISOK(pSC) 0 do $System.Status.DecomposeStatus(pSC, .tErr) set tHttp = +$Get(tErr(1, "param", 2)) Quit (tErr(1, "code") = ..GeneralCode()) && (tHttp >= 400) && (tHttp <= 599)

Method.name: Message
Method.Implementation: Quit:'..Carried(pSC) ..Text(pSC) do $System.Status.DecomposeStatus(pSC, .tErr) Quit $Get(tErr(1, "param", 1))

Method.name: Text
Method.Description: The readable text of <var>pSC</var>, without the "ERROR #5001: " prefix. A <tt>$$$GeneralError</tt> contributes its bare message; an ObjectScript error (with its routine offset) only the words "an unexpected internal error"; a datatype validation failure its text without the "ERROR #n: " prefix; any other error its usual one-line text. Several errors are joined with "; ".

Method.name: GeneralCode
Method.Description: Numeric code of <tt>$$$GeneralError</tt> as <tt>DecomposeStatus</tt> reports it.
Method.Implementation: $System.Status.GetErrorCodes($$$ERROR($$$GeneralError, ""))

Method.name: ObjectScriptCode
Method.Description: Numeric code of <tt>$$$ObjectScriptError</tt> (what a caught <UNDEFINED> becomes).
Method.Implementation: $System.Status.GetErrorCodes($$$ERROR($$$ObjectScriptError, ""))

Class.name: OPCUA.REST.Handler
Class.Description: REST dispatch handler for OPC UA adapter endpoints. Routes requests to service classes and formats consistent JSON responses.

Parameter.name: HandleCorsRequest
Parameter.Description: Enable CORS. The Angular console is served from a different origin than IRIS (localhost:4200 in development, and any static host in production), so every call it makes is cross-origin. Required, not vestigial.

Method.name: Login
Method.Description: Called by CSP when the request's IRIS sign-in failed (audit #16): answer 401 with the usual JSON envelope. This follows %CSP.REST.Login (CORS, and OPTIONS preflight allowed without sign-in) except that it sends no WWW-Authenticate header: a Basic challenge makes the browser open its own login dialog over the console, which has its own sign-in. Under the default setup this does not run. CSP calls it in the pre-login context (user CSPSystem, no roles), which cannot read the namespace's code database (%DB_OPCUA has no public permission). Loading this class then fails with <PROTECT>, and CSP answers a bare text/html 404 itself. That is IRIS's response, not ours; the console recognises it as a failed sign-in (see apiErrorMessage in the webapp). We deliberately do not grant that context read access (audit #16). The override stays because it is correct wherever the security context lets it run, and harmless otherwise.

XData.name: UrlMap
XData.Description: Route map — endpoints accept both GET and POST. POST with a JSON body is what the webapp uses, and the only practical way to pass a nested payload such as a schema's column list. GET with query parameters is kept because it makes an endpoint testable from a browser or curl without composing a body. `/schemas` is the exception: it uses real verbs, GET/POST/DELETE meaning list/create/delete on the same URL.

Method.name: Respond
Method.Description:
Send the response for a route: the data envelope on success, otherwise the error envelope with the HTTP status from <class>OPCUA.REST.Error</class>.
Mapping: bad input 400 (plain <tt>$$$GeneralError</tt>s and <method>OPCUA.REST.Error.BadRequest</method>), unknown schema or pipeline 404, conflict 409 (schema in use, name taken, another production running, edit lock busy, stale save), failed sign-in 401 (<method>Login</method>), anything else 500. 4xx responses carry our own message without the "ERROR #5001: " prefix.
A 500 never carries internal detail. The full error goes to the Interoperability event log (<method>LogInternal</method>) under a reference that the response quotes. An unexpected error answers "Internal error. Reference <ref>". A change that was saved but whose follow-up failed (the "... saved, but ..." errors from Rebind, Toggle and Delete) is a 500 built with <method>OPCUA.REST.Error.Make</method>: it shows its own message, so the console can say what was saved, plus the reference.

Method.name: LogInternal
Method.Description:
Write the text of an internal error to the Interoperability event log (Interoperability > View > Event Log, source OPCUA.REST.Handler).
Not the application error log: <tt>LOG^%ETN</tt> saves every stack frame's variables, the request body and its parsed objects among them, which would copy OPC UA passwords into <tt>^ERRORS</tt>. The event log entry holds only this text, and any password-like value from the request is masked in it first.

Method.Description: The non-empty values of every request field whose name contains "password", in the JSON body (at any depth) or the query string, as <var>pSecrets</var>(value).

Class.name: OPCUA.REST.PipelineService
Class.Description: Manage deployed OPC UA pipelines: list, toggle, delete, rebind. Reads and edits the shared production, OPCUA.Pipeline.Production (<method>OPCUA.REST.ProductionEdit.ProductionClass</method>).

Parameter.name: RowCountTTL
Parameter.Description:
How long a cached row count stays usable, in seconds.
Shorter than the dashboard's own 5s refresh would defeat the purpose; much longer and a freshly-started pipeline appears to collect nothing. Ten seconds means at most one table scan per two dashboard refreshes.

Method.name: List
Method.Description: List all pipeline service items with their runtime status.

Method.name: ListEntry
Method.Description: One pipeline's entry for <method>List</method>. Throws on an unexpected error, which List reports as that item's <tt>error</tt>.

Method.name: GetSettingValue
Method.Description: Get a setting value from a config item by name.

Method.name: GetHealth
Method.Description:
Classify a pipeline's real collection health, and report when it last did any work. The adapters already publish "OK" or "Error" per poll cycle via $$$SetHostMonitor; this reads that verdict back rather than inferring health from config, so a pipeline that is enabled but failing to connect, resolve, or read is reported as such. pHealth is one of:
  • stopped — the production is not running
  • disabled — the config item is switched off
  • error — running and retrying, but not collecting
  • ok — collecting normally
  • starting — enabled, but has not reported a cycle yet
pCycles is the number of completed cycles, or "" when the host has not reported any. It is what separates "just started" from "running dry".

Method.name: GetRowCount
Method.Description:
Get row count for a DataSource table, cached briefly.
The dashboard refreshes on a 5-second timer and calls this once per pipeline, so twenty pipelines over large tables was twenty full <tt>SELECT COUNT(*)</tt> scans every five seconds — a database cost driven entirely by a UI polling decision. A short TTL collapses that to one scan per table per window while keeping the number visibly live: rows accumulate over minutes, not milliseconds, so a few seconds of staleness in a count is not something an operator can perceive, whereas the scan cost is real.
Cached in <tt>^IRIS.Temp</tt> deliberately — it is derived data that should not survive a restart or be journalled.
Returns "" (unknown, null in the JSON) when the count cannot be taken, e.g. the class has no table or the user may not SELECT from it. 0 would read as "no rows", and the dashboard warns about a pipeline collecting nothing.

Method.name: GetNodeNames
Method.Description: Get the OPC UA node names from a DataSource class definition.

Method.name: Toggle
Method.Description: Toggle a pipeline service item on/off using Ens.Config API.

Method.name: Delete
Method.Description:
Delete a pipeline: remove its service item from the production.
The schema is deliberately left alone. A schema is a reusable asset that can back many pipelines, so deleting one pipeline must not destroy it — doing so would break every sibling still bound to it, and since the schema class owns the table, it would also discard the collected data.
Deleting a schema is <method>OPCUA.REST.SchemaService.Delete</method>, which refuses while any pipeline still references it.

Method.name: Rebind
Method.Description: Rebind an existing pipeline's device list. This is the whole of "editing a pipeline" once schema creation and device binding are separate concerns: the schema is fixed at deploy time, so a pipeline owns only which devices it reads. That is a config-item setting, so this needs no regeneration and no recompile. Changing a schema's columns is deliberately not possible here, and currently not possible anywhere — the regenerating edit path was removed with the wizard that drove it. Recreating the schema is the supported route. Body: { name required, devices required }

Method.name: DescribeItem
Method.Description:
Read the connection settings a pipeline was deployed with, so an operation on an existing pipeline can browse the same endpoint the same way.
Without the security settings a secured pipeline's coverage check would fail to connect and reject every device, so they are carried across rather than defaulted.

Method.name: CheckCanDeleteCredentials
Method.Description: 403 if pipeline <var>pItemName</var> owns a credentials entry (one deploy created for it) that this IRIS account may not delete. Read without the edit lock, so it runs before <method>Delete</method> touches anything.
Method.Implementation: set tProd = ##class(Ens.Config.Production).%OpenId(##class(OPCUA.REST.ProductionEdit).ProductionClass(), 0) Quit:'$IsObject(tProd) $$$OK set tItem = ##class(OPCUA.REST.ProductionEdit).FindItem(tProd, pItemName) Quit:'$IsObject(tItem) $$$OK set tCredId = ..GetSettingValue(tItem, "Credentials") Quit:'##class(OPCUA.REST.DeployService).OwnsCredentials(tCredId, pItemName) $$$OK Quit:##class(OPCUA.REST.DeployService).CanWriteCredentials() $$$OK Quit ##class(OPCUA.REST.Error).Forbidden("Pipeline '"_pItemName_"' was not deleted. "_##class(OPCUA.REST.Error).Text(##class(OPCUA.REST.DeployService).NoCredentialsAccess("delete its credentials '"_tCredId_"'", "W")))

Method.name: GetRowSourceInfo
Method.Description:
Describe a v2 pipeline's devices, from the DeviceNodePaths setting plus the schema class — the two places that now hold the truth.
Every device is reported with the schema's full column list, because a device's actual coverage is only known once it has been browsed at connect time; use POST /schemas/:name/validate for real per-device coverage.

Method.name: DeleteSerialSubclasses
Method.Description:
Delete serial object subclasses for a DataSource class. Scans the class's properties for types extending %SerialObject (excluding OPCUA.Types.*). Also called by <class>OPCUA.REST.SchemaService</class> when deleting a schema. Delete serial subclasses that belong to this schema and are not shared.
A serial class is deleted only if: 1. Its name matches SerialClassName(pClassName, <folder>) for some folder 2. No other compiled class (outside pClassName) has a property of that type
Returns %Status so errors propagate to SchemaService.Delete.

Method.Description: Check if a serial class is used by any class other than pMainClass.

Class.name: OPCUA.REST.ProductionEdit
Class.Description:
The one way the console changes the pipeline production. Every console read-modify-save of OPCUA.Pipeline.Production (deploy, toggle, delete, rebind) runs Begin, then its change, then Commit, then End:
  • Begin takes one named lock, ^OPCUA.ProductionEdit, with a timeout, so two console edits never interleave. A busy lock is refused at once with "in progress" rather than waiting forever.
  • Begin rereads the production from disk and records the production class's TimeChanged. Every SaveToClass moves it, the Portal's included.
  • Commit refuses if that stamp moved, so a Portal save made during our edit is not overwritten. Otherwise it runs %Save and SaveToClass once.
The Portal does not take our lock, and its own save checks no timestamp. Two gaps are therefore known and cannot be closed with documented APIs:
  1. A Portal save that lands in the millisecond window between Commit's stamp check and its SaveToClass is still overwritten in the class.
  2. A Portal page loaded before a console edit and saved after it overwrites the console's change. That is the Portal's code, so it can't be closed from our side.

Parameter.name: ProductionClass
Parameter.Description: The shared production class that holds all pipeline service items.

Parameter.name: LockTimeout
Parameter.Description: Seconds Begin waits for another console edit to finish.

Method.name: ProductionClass
Method.Description: The production being edited. Tests point this at a throwaway production through <tt>^||OPCUA.Tests("production")</tt>.
Method.Implementation: Quit $Get(^||OPCUA.Tests("production"), ..#ProductionClass)

Method.name: Begin
Method.Description:
Lock, reread the production, and record its change stamp.
On failure the lock is already released and <var>pProd</var> is "". On success the caller must call <method>End</method>.

Method.name: Commit
Method.Description: Save the production, unless someone saved it since <method>Begin</method>. Does not release the lock; call <method>End</method>.

Method.name: End
Method.Description: Release the edit lock. Harmless when it is not held.
Method.Implementation: lock -^OPCUA.ProductionEdit

Method.name: UpdateItem
Method.Description:
Change one config item in a single locked open and save.
<var>pSettings</var> is keyed by target, then setting name, for example <tt>{"Adapter":{"DeviceNodePaths":"..."}}</tt>. A setting the item lacks is added. <var>pFields</var> sets item properties, for example <tt>{"Category":"OPCUA,Line"}</tt>.

Method.name: FindItem
Method.Description: The item with exactly this name, or "". Walks the list rather than using <tt>FindItemByConfigName</tt>, which parses "Name|Class" syntax out of the name.

Method.name: SetSetting
Method.Description: Set a setting on an item, adding it when absent.

Method.name: Stamp
Method.Description:
The production class's last-change time (<tt>TimeChanged</tt>), read from the class dictionary on disk. Every SaveToClass moves it.
Read straight from the dictionary, not through SQL or <tt>%OpenId</tt>: dynamic SQL on <tt>%Dictionary.ClassDefinition</tt> needs a SELECT privilege the installer's OPCUA_API role does not grant (SQLCODE -99), and <tt>%OpenId</tt> can hand back a copy this process already holds.
Method.Implementation: Quit $$$defClassKeyGet(pClass, $$$cCLASStimechanged)

Method.name: ProductionStatus
Method.Description: The namespace's production name and state, with status. Tests stand in for a state they cannot force (Troubled) through <tt>^||OPCUA.Tests("productionStatus")</tt> as <tt>$LB(name, state)</tt>.

Method.name: ApplyToRunning
Method.Description:
Make a saved change take effect in the running production, and report honestly whether that happened.
<var>pRestarted</var> is 1 only when our production is running and <tt>UpdateProduction</tt> returned OK. When the production is not running at all there is nothing to update: the result is OK, <var>pRestarted</var> is 0 and <var>pNote</var> says why. When it is ours but suspended or troubled, or the update fails, the error says why. Callers prefix it with what was saved.

Class.name: OPCUA.REST.ReadService
Class.Description: Read a single OPC UA node value and return as JSON, typed from the node's DataType.

Method.name: Read
Method.Description: Read the value of a specified node. Input: pBody with url, nodeNs (default 0), nodeId (required), nodeIdType (default 0) Returns a %DynamicObject with value, timestamps, and inferred type.

Method.name: SafeReadAndParse
Method.Description: Perform the read, type inference, and result parsing in an isolated method. This ensures Try/Catch reliably catches $ZF errors from the C++ layer.

Method.name: SafeReadValue
Method.Description: Safely call ReadValueAttribute, catching any C++ layer exceptions. Returns the read's error, caught or not, so the caller can say why it failed.

Method.name: SafeExtractValue
