Class.name: OPCUA.REST.SchemaService
Class.Description:
Create and manage device schemas independently of any pipeline (PRD "Baustein 1", §4.9).
A schema is a compiled subclass of <class>OPCUA.DataSource.DeviceSchema</class> describing ONE device type: its columns and the OPC UA node names they resolve against. Creating one has no production, service-item or device-binding side effects — binding devices to a schema is a separate act, performed either by <class>OPCUA.REST.DeployService</class> or by hand in the Management Portal.
This class owns all schema *generation*; DeployService owns device *binding*.

Parameter.name: DefaultPackage
Parameter.Description: Default package for generated schemas, matching the wizard's convention.

Method.name: Create
List
Method.Description: GET /schemas — list every compiled schema with its column count, table name, and the pipelines currently bound to it.

Method.name: Get
Method.Description: GET /schemas/:name — column detail for one schema, used to drive device-binding validation in the UI.

Method.name: Delete
Method.Description: DELETE /schemas/:name — delete a schema and its generated serial subclasses. Refuses while any production config item still references it.

Method.name: Validate
Method.Description:
POST /schemas/:name/validate — dry run a device binding.
Browses the given device(s) and reports, per device, which of the schema's columns resolve and which do not. This is the mitigation for the deferred-failure risk that name-based resolution introduces: it moves the "does this device actually have these nodes?" question back to before deploy.
Body: schema name plus `devices` (newline-separated nodepaths, or an array) and the usual connection parameters (url, securityMode, certificates, ...).

Method.name: RequireUsableDevices
Method.Description:
Refuse a device list containing any device that would contribute nothing. A device only earns a place in a pipeline if the server answered its browse and at least one schema column matched. Both failures are rejected, for different reasons:
  • browsed, zero matches — the wrong node, or a leaf. Every row it produced would be entirely NULL, forever.
  • could not be browsed — unreachable, or the NodeId does not exist. Nothing can be verified, so the binding cannot be shown to be good.
This is a deploy-time gate only, and deliberately not enforced at runtime: a device that drops offline mid-session must keep storing NULL and warning, not take the pipeline down. Enforcing it on every connect would recreate StrictSchemaMatch, which was removed for exactly that reason. The cost is that a device cannot be bound before it exists. Adding it later is a rebind — one settings edit, no recompile. pSchemaClass is passed explicitly rather than read from pBody: on a deploy body `name` is the pipeline name, so resolving the schema from it would check the wrong class (or fail outright). Devices and connection parameters come from pBody. This reuses Validate so there is one definition of coverage.

Method.name: GenerateSchemaClass
Method.Description:
Generate and compile a device schema class, plus any %SerialObject classes its nested columns need. No production or device-binding side effects.
pColNamespaces(i) optionally overrides the OPC UA namespace for the column at 0-based index i; columns without an entry use pDefaultNS. This is how the wizard deploy path preserves the per-node namespaces it browsed.
pIncludeServerTS 0 types every measurement, flat or nested, as its OPCUA.Types.NoServerTS counterpart, which has no ServerTimeStamp property.

Method.name: GenerateSerialClasses
Method.Description:
Generate and compile %SerialObject classes for nested folder columns.
On any error, returns it with every class created so far recorded in pCreatedClasses, which tracks the classes created across both this method and the caller (GenerateSchemaClass). The caller's Catch deletes exactly those.

Method.name: SerialClassName
Method.Description:
Name of the %SerialObject class backing a nested folder.
An OPC UA browse name is free text, but a class name is not: underscores and most punctuation are rejected by %Dictionary.Classname validation, so the folder name is sanitised before it becomes an identifier. Without this, a folder called "State_Condition" fails the schema save with #5794 rather than producing a usable class.
The folder's real OPC UA name is preserved as the property's OPCUANODENAME, which is what resolution actually matches on — so sanitising here changes the class name only, never the name looked up on the device.
Method.Implementation: kill tUsed set tIdent = ##class(OPCUA.DataSource.Generator).SanitizePropertyName(pFolderName, .tUsed) set tIdent = $Replace(tIdent, "_", "") if tIdent = "" set tIdent = "Folder" // A leading digit survives sanitisation as "N<digits>", so only the empty // case needs guarding above. Quit pMainClassName_"."_tIdent_"Type"

Method.name: MapToDataValueType
Method.Description:
Preserve the OPC UA DataValue wrapper, including its status and timestamps. Plain type aliases remain accepted in API requests, but produce wrappers too. Unknown/unprobed types keep the existing string fallback.
pIncludeServerTS 0 returns the OPCUA.Types.NoServerTS counterpart instead. Either family is accepted as input and mapped to the requested one.
Method.Implementation: set tType = ..MapToFullDataValueType($Replace(pInferredType, "OPCUA.Types.NoServerTS.", "OPCUA.Types.", 1, 1)) Quit:pIncludeServerTS tType set tShort = "OPCUA.Types.NoServerTS."_$Extract(tType, 13, *) Quit $Select(##class(%Dictionary.CompiledClass).%ExistsId(tShort):tShort, 1:"OPCUA.Types.NoServerTS.StringDataValue")

Method.name: MapToFullDataValueType
Method.Description: Map an inferred type onto an OPCUA.Types measurement that keeps its server timestamp.

Method.name: FindDefaultNamespace
Method.Description: Find the most common namespace among a set of nodes (or columns).

Method.Description: Add a parameter to a class definition.

Method.Description:
Resolve the target class name from `className`, or from `name` plus an optional `packagePath` (defaulting to OPCUA.DS).
The result must be a valid class name, so a bad name is a 400 saying so here, rather than a %Dictionary datatype error later.

Method.name: RequireSchema
Method.Description: Resolve and validate that the requested schema exists and really is a schema.

Method.name: IsSchema
Method.Description: Is this class a usable device schema?

Method.name: DescribeSchema
Method.Description:
Describe one schema: identity, table, and (optionally) its columns. Columns are reported in storage order, which is the order the runtime services and the resolver's coverage masks use.
<var>pSC</var> is the error when the columns cannot be read (e.g. the class's compiled spec in <tt>^OPCUA.DataSource</tt> is missing); the item then has <tt>columnCount</tt> 0 and a <tt>columnsError</tt> saying why.

Method.name: MapSchemaUsage
Method.Description:
Map usage across ALL productions in the namespace.
Output: pUsage(schemaClass, production, itemName) = "". Any failure (e.g. cannot open a production) is returned as a %Status error, so callers can refuse actions that depend on complete usage information.
Not private: PipelineService reports remaining usage after deleting a pipeline, and this is the single definition of "which pipelines use what".

Method.name: UsageArray
Method.Description:
Turn the three-subscript usage map into a JSON array of objects.
Input: pUsage(schemaClass, production, itemName) = "" Output: [{name: itemName, production: prodClass, managed: true|false}, ...] where managed = true if production is OPCUA.Pipeline.Production.

set tArr = [] set tProdClass = "" for { set tProdClass = $Order(pUsage(pSchemaClass, tProdClass)) quit:tProdClass=""
set tItemName = "" for { set tItemName = $Order(pUsage(pSchemaClass, tProdClass, tItemName)) quit:tItemName=""
set tObj = {} set tObj.name = tItemName set tObj.production = tProdClass set tManaged = (tProdClass = ##class(OPCUA.REST.DeployService).#ProductionClass) do tObj.%Set("managed", tManaged, "boolean") do tArr.%Push(tObj) } } Quit tArr

A business service that uses the TCPPollingInboundAdapter to poll data from multiple OPC UA devices sharing the same device schema, producing one row per device per poll cycle. Each row includes a NodePath column identifying the source device.
The device list comes from the adapter's DeviceNodePaths setting, and each device's nodes are resolved by name at connect time (see <class>OPCUA.DataSource.Resolver</class>). Devices may have partial column coverage: a column with no matching node on a given device is stored as NULL and logged. Adding a device is therefore a one-line setting edit — no regeneration, no recompile.

The device list comes from the adapter's DeviceNodePaths setting, and each device's nodes are resolved by name at connect time (see <class>OPCUA.DataSource.Resolver</class>). Devices may have partial column coverage: a column with no matching node on a given device is stored as NULL and logged.

Class.name: OPCUA.Types.Multidimensional
Class.Description:
A multi-dimensional value may have a number of dimensions. If it has just one dimension, consider using the Array types which are typed and can be easily iterated using the normal %Collection methods such as Count() and GetAt().
But if it has more than one dimension, this is the perfect type for it. To keep things simple though, we are not enforcing the data type in the IRIS side. The "Values" property is just a %List (A $listbuild) that is actually a "list of lists". If you have two dimensions, each element of this list is another list like: Example for getting row 1, column 1: $ListGet($ListGet(obj.Values, 1), 1). If you have three dimensions, this will be $ListGet($ListGet($ListGet(obj.Values, 1) , 1), 1).

Class.name: OPCUA.Types.NoServerTS.AbstractDataValue
Class.Description:
A measurement without its ServerTimeStamp: source timestamp, status and the typed payload. Device schemas created with includeServerTimestamp = false type their columns with the classes in this package, so their tables have no *_ServerTimeStamp column at all.
This deliberately does not extend <class>OPCUA.Types.AbstractDataValue</class>, which would bring the property back. Each concrete class mirrors its OPCUA.Types counterpart (OPCUA.Types.X is OPCUA.Types.NoServerTS.X here) with the payload starting at storage position 3 instead of 4.
The native layer always returns the full DataValue, so only <class>OPCUA.DataSource.RowWriter</class>, which drops the server timestamp, may store these. Hand-authored DataSources under TCPPollingService store the native list unchanged and must keep using the OPCUA.Types classes.

Method.Description:
Run dynamic SQL and return its result set, throwing if the statement failed. <tt>%ExecDirect</tt> reports a failure (a missing table, a missing SELECT privilege) in the result's <tt>%SQLCODE</tt> rather than by throwing, so a caller that only checks <tt>$IsObject</tt> reads a failed query as an empty one.
A missing privilege (SQLCODE -99) throws <method>OPCUA.REST.Error.Forbidden</method>, a readable 403, rather than an opaque 500: signing in again does not help, an administrator has to grant it.
